clue.text: 'Horace .. favouring Alice with a languishing ——' (Frank Smedley, Henry Coverdale's Courtship)

definitions.text: 'Horace .. favouring Alice with a languishing ——' (Frank Smedley, Henry Coverdale's Courtship)

parts.words: 'Horace .. favouring Alice with a languishing ——' (Frank Smedley, Henry Coverdale's Courtship)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing word is a French-derived term for an amorous, lingering glance

explanation.surface: A line from a Victorian novel in which Horace gives Alice a lovesick look.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word means an ogle or wink, the languishing look a suitor casts.

clue.text: Edgar's serviceable villain

parts.note: in King Lear Edgar kills Goneril's steward and calls him 'a serviceable villain'

explanation.surface: A villain who is useful to someone named Edgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril's officious steward in King Lear is described by Edgar with exactly this phrase.

clue.text: O'Neill's killer

parts.note: points to Eugene O'Neill's play The ... Cometh, where the ... stands for death

explanation.surface: A man named O'Neill turns murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: In O'Neill's play the coming iceman is a figure for death, the killer every barfly awaits.

clue.text: Alcott characters first encountered by Gulliver?

definitions.meaning: Louisa May Alcott's sequel to Little Women is about the boys of Plumfield
the Lilliputians, tiny people, were the first race Gulliver met

explanation.definitionFit: Alcott's Plumfield boys give a book title, and Swift's Lilliputians are tiny people Gulliver meets first.

clue.text: Decorating space where actors prepare

parts.note: dressing a shop window or a tree is decorating it
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A space being decorated backstage for the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers change costume and apply make-up in the backstage chamber set aside for them.

clue.text: Defoe's fortunate mistress

parts.note: points to the 1724 Defoe novel subtitled The Fortunate Mistress, named for its heroine

explanation.surface: A lucky courtesan in the writings of Daniel Defoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's novel bears the subtitle The Fortunate Mistress, and its heroine takes this name.

clue.text: Circle wagon for Prince of Wales

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: Drawing wagons into a circle for the Welsh prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Owain Glyndwr was the last native Welshman to hold the title Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndwr, the medieval Welsh leader, proclaimed himself Prince of Wales.

clue.text: Ancient city under royal publishing ban

definitions.meaning: a Philistine city on the coast of Canaan
King David's lament says 'publish it not in the streets of' this city

explanation.definitionFit: A Philistine coastal town, named in David's lament: tell it not in Gath, publish it not in its streets.

clue.text: The entire Orient bloodstained in symbolical narrative

parts.note: all means the entire amount
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: The whole East soaked in blood, told as a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A story whose characters and events stand for hidden moral or political meanings.

clue.text: Way Ethel reformed authority on satanism

indicators.note: formed again, so the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: Ethel's way of life has been reformed by an expert in devil worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Wheatley wrote popular occult thrillers such as The Devil Rides Out.
explanation.definitionFit: The thriller novelist Dennis Wheatley was famous for black-magic stories and was treated as an expert on the occult.

clue.text: Her papers were compiled by Martin Amis

definitions.text: Her papers were compiled by Martin Amis

parts.words: Her papers were compiled by Martin Amis
parts.note: refers to Amis's first novel, The ... Papers, named after its heroine

explanation.surface: Martin Amis edits a woman's archive.
explanation.definitionFit: Amis's 1973 debut is The Rachel Papers, so the woman whose papers he compiled is its title girl.

clue.text: One of 27, perhaps — The Pilot's Arms of Chesterton?

definitions.text: One of 27, perhaps — The Pilot's Arms of Chesterton?

parts.words: One of 27, perhaps — The Pilot's Arms of Chesterton?
parts.note: a Chesterton novel title that sounds like a pub name, an airman's tavern

explanation.surface: Chesterton names a pub after aviators.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's 1914 novel about defiant innkeepers has a title that would suit a pub for airmen.

clue.text: Some terribly allergic thriller writer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer of thrillers who suffers dreadful allergies.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavin Lyall was a British author of aviation and spy thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin Lyall wrote suspense novels such as The Wrong Side of the Sky.

clue.text: Composer from beautiful mountain in Germany

parts.note: the German word for beautiful is schön, written without the umlaut
the German word for mountain is Berg

explanation.surface: A composer inspired by a lovely German peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Germany' tells you both pieces are German words.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg, often spelt this way, was the Austrian pioneer of twelve-tone music.

clue.text: Reliable fellow identified by Maugham and Eggleston

definitions.meaning: a trustworthy man who keeps his word
Somerset Maugham's early play and Edward Eggleston's novel share this title

explanation.definitionFit: A trustworthy person keeps his word; the phrase is also the title of works by both writers.

clue.text: Eucharistic offerings — uniquely to albinos?

indicators.note: in a unique, unusual way, so these words' letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Communion gifts presented only to albino worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: The bread and wine presented at Communion are gifts offered to God.

clue.text: Suitable setting for Walters spine-chiller

parts.note: Minette Walters's debut crime novel takes its title from a cold storage building; 'chiller' suits it

explanation.surface: A fitting location for a Minette Walters thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Walters's first novel is named after a storage building for keeping things frozen, apt for a chiller.

clue.text: Democratic decree, derived from the stones of Athens

definitions.text: Democratic decree, derived from the stones of Athens

parts.words: Democratic decree, derived from the stones of Athens
parts.note: Athenians voted with pebbles, and the Greek word for pebble gives this term for a decree passed by vote

explanation.surface: A law of the people traced back to Athenian stones.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian assembly resolution carried by voters casting pebbles, from Greek psephos, pebble.

clue.text: Easily croon a medley in gambling venue

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of these words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A singer croons a medley of songs without effort at the gaming tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the title of Ian Fleming's first James Bond novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional casino at Royale-les-Eaux is a gaming house where Bond plays baccarat.

clue.text: Dr Roffey's mad pet (Coward suggests)

parts.note: a sporting retriever; 'Coward suggests' points to the shy dog that flinches at shots

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps a crazed animal, as a playwright hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever or pointer trained to work with shooters is a sporting breed kept as a pet.

clue.text: Godwin and Horgan saw them as they are

definitions.text: Godwin and Horgan saw them as they are

parts.words: Godwin and Horgan saw them as they are
parts.note: Godwin's Caleb Williams is subtitled ... as They Are, and Paul Horgan wrote a novel of that title

explanation.surface: Two writers who see the world realistically.
explanation.definitionFit: Both writers used the title phrase about matters seen realistically, as they really stand.

clue.text: Mythological king, a victim of Heracles, from new Chopin op. ("0")

definitions.text: Mythological king, a victim of Heracles

indicators.note: new tells you the letters are made afresh in another order

parts.note: op. is the usual abbreviation for opus, a numbered musical work
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A new Chopin opus numbered zero tells the story of a legendary king.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippocoon of Sparta and his sons were killed by Heracles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this Spartan ruler was slain by Heracles for usurping his brother's throne.

clue.text: Brian's's was golden

parts.note: refers to Patrick O'Brian's novel The Golden ...

explanation.surface: Something of Brian's was made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue looks mangled; it means O'Brian's, author of The Golden Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick O'Brian's early sea novel is The Golden Ocean, about Anson's voyage round the world.

clue.text: Terry Pratchett told it, as did Zola, some of the time

definitions.text: Terry Pratchett told it, as did Zola, some of the time

parts.words: Terry Pratchett told it, as did Zola, some of the time
parts.note: 'some of the time' plays on telling it only occasionally

explanation.surface: Two novelists who were honest only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Pratchett's newspaper novel and Zola's last novel Vérité both take honesty as their title.

clue.text: "And, in the lawful name of marrying, / To give our hearts — ceremony " (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

definitions.text: "And, in the lawful name of marrying, / To give our hearts — ceremony " (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

parts.words: "And, in the lawful name of marrying, / To give our hearts — ceremony " (The Merry Wives of Windsor)
parts.note: a Shakespeare quotation to complete with the word Fenton uses for hearts joined in marriage

explanation.surface: A line from Fenton in Shakespeare's comedy about marrying for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts joined by the marriage ceremony are made one, which is the missing word's sense.

clue.text: Moderate republican from French department

definitions.meaning: a member of the moderate faction of the French Revolution
named after the Gironde, the department round Bordeaux whose deputies led it

explanation.definitionFit: The Revolutionary faction opposed to the Jacobins took its name from deputies of the Gironde region.

clue.text: Demons exorcised by Thackeray

indicators.note: demons driven out are thrown about, so this word's letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Thackeray drives out evil spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The History of Henry Esmond is Thackeray's historical novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's 1852 novel The History of Henry Esmond is usually known by its hero's surname.

clue.text: O'Casey's Rose and Crown, Jameson's Green Man and Stout's Red Bull, for example?

definitions.text: O'Casey's Rose and Crown, Jameson's Green Man and Stout's Red Bull, for example?

parts.words: O'Casey's Rose and Crown, Jameson's Green Man and Stout's Red Bull, for example?
parts.note: each literary title is also a common pub name, shown on the board hung outside a tavern

explanation.surface: A list of book titles by O'Casey, Jameson and Rex Stout.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose and Crown, Green Man and Red Bull are classic British pub names painted on hanging boards.
